title: Why the Neanderthals vanished
summary: Neanderthals disappeared around 40,000 years ago, perhaps later in Iberia. The cause is not settled; multiple factors likely hit an already small population.
why: They were our closest relatives; their end tells us what gave modern humans the edge, or luck.
question: Why did the Neanderthals die out about 40,000 years ago?
evidence: Extinction about 40,000 years ago; possible Iberian survival to about 35,000 disputed; overlap with modern humans, interbreeding, and cold dry phases all documented.
wouldSettle: Finely dated regional records showing which pressure coincided with each local disappearance.

theories.name: Replacement by modern humans
theories.idea: A more efficient incoming population out-competed them for resources.

theories.name: Climate swings
theories.idea: Cold, dry periods shrank their habitats and populations.

theories.name: Small-population problems
theories.idea: Inbreeding in small isolated groups and dilution through interbreeding eroded populations.

theories.name: Disease from newcomers
theories.idea: Modern humans brought diseases against which Neanderthals had no immunity.
